title: Kamaraj and the Electric Fan: Grounded Governance
culture_region: India / Greece / USA / South Africa / World
summary: Refusing special VIP amenities, Kamaraj switched off the fan: 'Bring electricity to the entire village first; then I will enjoy the fan alongside my people.'
keywords: Kamaraj and the Electric Fan: Grounded Governance
full_text:
During his nine years as Chief Minister, K. Kamaraj traveled constantly through rural Tamil Nadu without security convoys or VIP protocol.

On a blistering summer afternoon, Kamaraj stopped at a modest government inspection bungalow in an interior hamlet.

As he entered the room, an engineer started a loud portable diesel generator, sending cool air whirring from a large table fan directly onto the Chief Minister.

Kamaraj looked out the window. Across the dusty street, thatched huts stood baking under the sun; there were no electric poles or wires in sight.

Kamaraj called the engineer:
"Young man, does this village have electric power?"

The engineer beamed proudly: "No, sir, the main grid hasn't reached here yet. But because the Chief Minister was visiting, we specially brought a generator and fan from the city for your comfort!"

Kamaraj walked over to the wall switch and clicked the fan off!

Looking at the flustered officer, Kamaraj spoke with gentle authority:
"Turn off the generator!
The villagers are sweating in the scorching heat without a whisper of breeze. How can a Chief Minister sit under a fan in their midst?
Only when I sweat alongside my people will I remember their suffering!
Laying power lines to this entire village must be your first priority.
The day every hut here gets electricity, come back and switch on this fan for me! Now, let it be!"

Within three months, electric poles were erected, and power illuminated every home in the hamlet.

Kamaraj demonstrated that true leadership is sharing the hardship of the common man until justice is delivered to all.
moral: Privilege alienates leaders from reality; sharing the burdens of the people is the only path to meaningful governance.
